counterfactual_missing_items: He denied fever, cough, joint pain, or other systemic symptoms
There was no palpable cervical, axillary, or facial lymphadenopathy
absence of a painful undermined violaceous ulcer edge that would favor pyoderma gangrenosum
decisive_items: multiple papules and pustules on an erythematous base over the nasal dorsum, some with superficial ulceration and yellow crusting
papules and pustules on his nose
He had been treated with systemic and topical antibiotics at a local hospital without improvement
response.rationale: R1 best covers the full nasal morphology: papules/pustules on an erythematous base with superficial ulceration and crusting, combined with lack of systemic features and antibiotic failure. R4 shares the erythematous papulopustular nasal pattern but omits the ulceration/crusting and does not explain antibiotic non-response. R2 relies on trauma and ulceration but lacks the typical painful undermined violaceous PG ulcer; R3 and R5 capture only sparse papule/pustule wording and are disfavored by no systemic symptoms, no lymphadenopathy, and no response to antibiotics.

rejected.why: Prior trauma and ulceration/crusting are nonspecific; PG requires painful undermining violaceous ulcers, which are not described.
Only papules and pustules on the nose are captured; no follicle-centered lesions and no improvement with antibiotics argue against folliculitis.
Shared only by sparse papule/pustule wording; absence of systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy plus pustules and ulceration are atypical for sarcoidosis.
